title: The Postman's Fifty Centimes That Helped Build the Institut Pasteur
conflicts: Totals agree (more than 2.5 million by January 1888; 2,586,680 francs at the opening), but Vallery-Radot does not make clear whether parliament's 200,000-franc grant is inside that total, so the story says only that the accounts also recorded it. Pasteur's 350-treated, one-death figure is his own; the Science History Institute notes his notebooks show exaggerated published results, which the story states. The Tsar's 100,000 francs is from Vallery-Radot only.
notes: Slate year 1887 is the charitable-status decree; the episode runs from the March 1886 appeal to the November 1888 opening. Vallery-Radot was Pasteur's son-in-law; his book is used for documented events, letters and speeches.
